videos.script: A forecast is three answers, and most reports give only one of them. {{three}} The first is the number. Next week, ten thousand orders. {{number}} The second is how far ahead it reaches. A number for next week and a number for next December are not equally good, and nobody should treat them alike. {{horizon}} The third is how wrong it might be. Ten thousand, give or take three hundred, is a different promise from ten thousand, give or take three thousand. {{interval}} And there is a fourth thing, which is time. Next month the same forecast will be made again, with a month more data, and it will say something different. {{revision}} That is not the forecast failing. That is the forecast working. The failure is pretending the old number never existed. {{record}} This lesson takes Panela's forecasts from lesson 3 and asks of each one: how far, how sure, and what changed. {{end}}
